source.name: BBC World News RSS
source.title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
source.summary: The WMO has warned that the natural weather phenomenon could bring disruption to global economies.
source.evidence_text:
The UN warned that the developing El Niño could be exceptionally strong.
El Niño is a natural Pacific Ocean process involving changed winds, warmer water spreading eastward and heat released into the air.
The event can alter rainfall, leaving some regions unusually dry and others exposed to heavier rain and floods.
The WMO warned of possible harm to communities and economic activity worldwide.
Governments and scientists were preparing responses, including improved warnings and medical support.
The WMO was working to distribute forecasts of possible extreme weather to communities.
Australia had introduced warning systems to help respond to threats to marine life and fisheries.
The report described global warming as an additional influence that could intensify the impacts.
Forecasters expected below-normal rainfall in substantial parts of South East Asia and Central America.
Forecasts pointed to increased rainfall in parts of eastern Africa and southern Brazil.
source.evidence_kind: Editor-written factual notes paraphrased from the linked BBC article; not quotations or independent reporting.

lesson.title: A weather warning
lesson.overview: Notice the difference between a warning and a certainty.
lesson.prediction: Read the title. What do you think the story is about?
discussion: What happened? Start with: The report says ___.
Imagine bad weather tomorrow. Complete: I could prepare by ___.
news_brief_sentences: The UN has warned about a very strong El Niño.
This natural weather event starts in the Pacific Ocean.
It can bring less rain to some places and more rain to others.
It could cause disruption to economies around the world.
Countries are preparing by improving weather warnings.
Some are also getting medical help ready for people who may need it.

grammar.explanation: Could cause describes a possible result. It does not say that the result is certain.

quiz.question: What are countries doing?
options: Preparing for possible effects
Declaring that there can be no effects
Reporting that El Niño has never happened
option_feedback: The headline says countries are preparing.
Preparing does not mean ruling out all effects.
The source does not make this historical claim.

quiz.question: What does disruption mean?
options: A problem that interrupts normal activity
A promise that everything will improve
A fixed date for a meeting
option_feedback: Disruption interferes with normal activity.
Improvement is not the meaning of disruption.
Disruption does not name a date.

quiz.question: Which keeps the warning uncertain?
options: It could cause problems.
It will certainly cause problems.
It has caused every problem.
option_feedback: Could preserves a possibility.
Certainly changes the warning into a certainty.
This adds an unsupported past claim about every problem.
